question: What stops old steel from being recycled into the best new steel?
answer: Copper. Shredded cars bring wiring and motors into the scrap, and steelmaking cannot remove copper: being less reactive than iron, it stays in the melt instead of passing into the slag. A fraction of a per cent makes steel crack when rolled hot, so contaminated scrap ends up in reinforcing bar, not in car doors.
move: A material recycles only as well as its worst passenger can be removed.
source: Daehn et al., Environmental Science & Technology, 2017
reference: Daehn, Cabrera Serrenho & Allwood, How Will Copper Contamination Constrain Future Global Steel Recycling?, Environmental Science & Technology, 2017
